assessment: Within this manuscript the authors set out to determine the biogenesis of c-type cytochromes in methane producing archaea called methanogens. Compared to the bacterical cytochrome c assembly system, genes like ccmD, ccmH and ccmI are not found in archaea that contain a functional cytochrome Cs. They show that the proteins encoded by the ccmABCEF genes of Methanosarcina acetivorans are both essential and sufficient for cyt c biogenesis. They also show the substrate specific role of the mmcA y cyt c M. acetivorans. The authors do this using a combination of genetic, molecular, and physiological and biochemical analyses. These data are of high interest of scientists working on bioenergetics and yt c biogenesis in archaea.
